speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the underlying driving force for the recent spate of en bloc sales of properties; (b) whether there is a need for the Government to ramp up its land sales to meet developers' demand for land; and (c) what is the impact of the recent demand on the outlook for the property market for the next six months.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There has been a healthy increase in the sales of new units in the first three quarters of the year which, in turn, means that the unsold supply in the pipeline has come down.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, because the numbers of unsold units have come down, developers are keen to replenish their land banks, and that has contributed in part to more en bloc sales.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The supply of these new units from en bloc sales, as well as other factors, such as population and income growth, and property market conditions, will be taken into consideration in deciding the quantum of land to be put out for Government Land Sales (GLS).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The GLS programme is updated on a half-yearly basis with sites on the Confirmed List, which means that the site will be released for sale within the next six months; as well as sites on the Reserve List which means that the sale of the site can be initiated by a developer, if they assess that there is demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will continue to monitor the overall trends and developments closely and take appropriate actions to maintain a stable and sustainable property market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is something that, I believe, many people have also expressed similar feedback and concerns on.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I would say, firstly, that the bids that the developers have put up for the en bloc sales, and you see the high bids that have been put up, need not necessarily translate into higher sales prices down the road.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is something that people are concerned about – that the developers bid high for land and, eventually, this would translate into higher prices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That need not happen because what the developers are able to sell for their units will eventually have to depend on the demand and supply conditions of the property market at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That would put some pressure on them to sell at a reasonable price within the five-year timeframe, otherwise, they would be subject to ABSD.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Eventually, we have to let the developers price their housing projects on a business or commercial basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But they understand that these are market conditions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is an ABSD regime in place, and we will monitor carefully to see what happens in the market down the road.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The other point that I would like to add is that, as I had mentioned earlier, the en bloc sites that are taken off the market now will eventually be put back into the market in the next one to two years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That will also put some moderating pressure on prices down the road.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Having said all that, like I have mentioned earlier, the Government continues to monitor the overall property market trends very closely.
